newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 6.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
- U.S. vehicle sales increased 2.2 percent in October, below expectations.
- U.S. retail and wholesale prices fell on news that refiners were producing heating oil at near record levels.
- Stock prices rose as the market anticipated a Democratic victory in the country's presidential elections and a Republican one in the House of Representatives.
- Bond prices rose on data revealing a weaker economy and stronger dollar.
- Civil rights groups urged the U.S. government to join a racial discrimination lawsuit against Texaco Inc.
- The National Association of Securities Dealers appears to be seeking a compromise as it devises new rules for arbitration procedures.
- Advertising agency Citron Haligman Bedecarre is launching a campaign to promote the mutual fund, Dreyfus.
- The travel industry is preparing for the arrival of the next century. Cruise ships are accepting reservations for New Year's Eve in 1999.
- Boston Properties is building its first speculative office project in seven years in the city.
- Brewer Pabst closes its plant after more than 150 years in operation.
